question: What is another common medical name for a pressure sore?
explanation: You'll often hear pressure sores called decubitus ulcers because patients used to mostly get them while lying down in bed. Good to know for your exams! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h1)

question: Where do pressure sores typically develop on the body?
explanation: Think about where bones push closest to the skin—like the heels or hips. When those spots press against a mattress too long, blood flow stops and sores form there first. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h1)

question: When a patient lies flat on their back, which body part is most at risk for a pressure sore?
explanation: The sacrum (lower back/tailbone area) carries a lot of weight when someone lies flat on their back. Always check this spot during your ward rounds! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h2)

question: A patient uses a wheelchair for most of the day. Which area needs your attention the most during skin checks?
explanation: When sitting, the weight of the upper body presses directly down on the ischial tuberosities (the sitting bones in the pelvis). That's why wheelchair users need special cushions! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h2)

question: What physical force happens when a patient's skin rubs roughly against bed sheets?
explanation: Friction is simply the scraping force when two things rub together—like skin sliding across rough bed sheets, which can easily peel away the top layer of skin. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h3)

question: Why does poor nutrition put a patient at a higher risk for pressure sores?

options.A: It causes immediate moisture accumulation on the epidermis
options.B: It impairs tissue healing and reduces skin resilience
options.C: It eliminates the protective padding of bony prominences
options.D: It directly increases the capillary closing pressure

explanation: Good food gives the body building blocks. Without enough protein and nutrients, the skin becomes weak, thin, and unable to repair itself quickly. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h3)

question: Which pressure sore stage has intact skin with redness that does not turn white (blanch) when you press it?
explanation: A Stage 1 pressure injury is the earliest warning sign. The skin isn't broken yet, but that red patch that stays red under your finger means the tissue underneath is already struggling. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h4)

question: You notice an open wound with exposed bone and deep tissue damage on a patient's heel. How would you classify this?
explanation: When you can see or touch bone, tendon, or muscle, it is automatically a Stage 4 pressure injury—the deepest and most severe category. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h4)

question: What is the main goal of debridement when managing a pressure sore?

options.A: Providing a pleasant scent to the room

explanation: Debridement means clearing away the dead (necrotic) tissue. Bacteria love to hide in dead tissue, so cleaning it out is the best way to let healthy new skin grow. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h5)

question: Why do nurses encourage high protein intake for patients with pressure ulcers?

options.A: It reduces the risk of joint contractures
options.B: It prevents the accumulation of wound exudate
options.C: It acts as a systemic anti-inflammatory agent
options.D: It supports tissue repair and cellular regeneration

explanation: Think of protein as the bricks and mortar for wound healing. The body needs those extra amino acids to rebuild damaged skin and flesh. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h5)

question: How often should you normally turn or reposition a patient who is confined to bed?
explanation: The golden rule of pressure care: turn bedbound patients at least every two hours to give their skin a break from constant pressure! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of using the Braden Scale in the hospital ward?

options.A: Measuring the exact surface area of an open wound
options.B: Assessing a patient's risk for pressure ulcer development
options.C: Evaluating the level of pain caused by a skin lesion
options.D: Determining the correct stage of a decubitus ulcer

explanation: The Braden Scale helps you spot patients who are in danger of getting sores *before* the damage even starts, checking things like moisture, mobility, and nutrition. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h6)
